axes.label: Entity type
axes.description: What kind of thing the entry is. The atlas mixes hardware, ideas, people, and organizations on purpose — they only make sense together.

values.label: Hardware
values.description: Chips, devices, architectures, boards. Loihi, TrueNorth, SpiNNaker, memristor crossbars, event cameras.

values.label: Algorithm
values.description: Training methods, learning rules, encodings, simulators. Surrogate gradients, STDP, rate vs temporal coding, Nengo.

values.label: Application
values.description: A concrete use case or demo that made the field credible (or didn't). Keyword spotting, event-based vision, robotic control, olfaction.

values.label: Organization
values.description: Labs, companies, consortia, funding programs. Intel Neuromorphic Lab, BrainChip, Innatera, Human Brain Project, DARPA SyNAPSE.

values.label: Person
values.description: Researchers and founders who shaped the field. Carver Mead, Misha Mahowald, Giacomo Indiveri, Mike Davies.

values.label: Concept
values.description: Foundational ideas: sparse coding, event-driven computation, in-memory compute, the memory wall, biological plausibility.

axes.label: Approach
axes.description: How the work implements (or sidesteps) neuromorphic computation. For people and organizations, the approach they primarily work on.

values.label: Digital
values.description: Clocked, deterministic spiking hardware or software. Loihi, TrueNorth, SpiNNaker.

values.label: Mixed-signal
values.description: Analog compute with digital communication. DYNAP, BrainScaleS, most academic neuromorphic chips.

values.label: Analog
values.description: Fully analog computation, typically with memristive or floating-gate devices. Mythic, memristor crossbars.

values.label: Photonic
values.description: Optical neuromorphic — light as the compute substrate. Lightmatter-adjacent research, photonic SNNs.

values.label: Software
values.description: Simulators, frameworks, training stacks that run on conventional hardware. Nengo, Brian2, snnTorch, Lava.

values.label: Theory
values.description: Not tied to a substrate: learning rules, coding schemes, computational neuroscience models, biological plausibility arguments.

axes.label: Motivation
axes.description: Why the work exists. The field is a coalition of people who want different things from the same silicon — this axis surfaces the disagreement. Pick the primary driver.

values.label: Neuroscience
values.description: Understand the brain. Hardware as a faster-than-real-time simulation substrate. Human Brain Project, BrainScaleS, most academic biophysical work.

values.label: Efficiency
values.description: Beat von Neumann on joules per inference. The commercial pitch: edge AI, always-on sensing, battery-bound devices. BrainChip, Innatera, most startups.

values.label: General intelligence
values.description: Brain-like computation as a path to flexible, general-purpose AI. Numenta historically, parts of the Loihi research community, cognitive architectures.

values.label: Scaling
values.description: Break the memory wall. In-memory and analog compute as a post-Moore substrate for any workload, not just SNNs. Memristor crowd, Mythic, IBM analog AI.

values.label: Robotics
values.description: Real-time sensorimotor loops, event-driven sensing, low-latency control. Prophesee / iniLabs lineage, ETH Zurich, drone and prosthetics work.

values.label: Bio-interface
values.description: Neural prosthetics, brain-computer interfaces, closed-loop biomedical devices. Retinal implants, cochlear-adjacent work, some Indiveri-group projects.

axes.label: Maturity
axes.description: How close the entry is to being a real thing people use. For people and organizations, the maturity of their most prominent output.

values.label: Theoretical
values.description: On paper or in simulation only. No silicon, no demo.

values.label: Lab demo
values.description: Working in a single lab, on a single chip, for a single benchmark. Not reproducible outside the group.

values.label: Prototype
values.description: Hardware or software available to outside collaborators. Multiple groups have used it. Still pre-product.

values.label: Commercial
values.description: A product is being sold or licensed. May or may not have real users at scale.

values.label: Deployed
values.description: In a shipping device or running workload that someone depends on. Rare in this field — that's the point.

values.label: Abandoned
values.description: Discontinued, defunded, or quietly shelved. The graveyard cells: IBM TrueNorth, Qualcomm Zeroth, various startups.

axes.label: Region
axes.description: Where the work is centered. The EU, US, and Asia funded neuromorphic on different terms and the lineages stayed somewhat separate.

values.label: US
values.description: United States. DARPA SyNAPSE, Intel, IBM, Stanford, academic labs across the country.

values.label: EU
values.description: Continental Europe. Human Brain Project, BrainScaleS (Heidelberg), Manchester-adjacent collaborations, ETH Zurich's Institute of Neuroinformatics.

values.label: UK
values.description: United Kingdom. SpiNNaker (Manchester), Cambridge, Sussex.

values.label: Asia
values.description: China, Japan, Korea, Singapore, India. Tianjic, Darwin, growing commercial activity.

values.label: Other
values.description: Australia, Canada, Israel, anywhere else.
